title: "Lecture 9 — Self-check answers"
sidebar: mfml
---

1. $P_{X}(x)=\int_{-\infty}^{x}p_{X}(t)\,dt$ (when a density exists).
2. Densities are not probabilities; only integrals over sets are. Normalization constrains the integral to $1$, not point values to $[0,1]$.
3. $p(x)=2$ on $[0,1/2]$. The value $2$ cannot be a probability, so PDF evaluations are not probabilities — even though Gaussians often look $\le 1$.
4. For discrete RVs: the PMF value $p(x)=P(X=x)$ is a probability. Not for continuous PDFs.
5. From “estimate the distribution” to “estimate the density” (joints/marginals/conditionals), assuming densities exist for our data.
